31982102.title: 1982_Los_Angeles_Rams–Green_Bay_Packers_game
31982102.extract:
## Background

The 1982 NFL season followed a 57-day players' strike that canceled games from September 21 to November 15, reducing the schedule from 16 to nine games per team and expanding the playoffs to include eight teams per conference. This game occurred in Week 1, before the strike began.

The Los Angeles Rams entered the season under head coach Ray Malavasi, who had led the team since 1978. In 1981, the Rams finished with a 6–10 record, missing the playoffs after reaching the Super Bowl two years earlier. The team relied on running back Wendell Tyler, who had rushed for 1,109 yards the previous season, and quarterback Bert Jones, acquired in a trade from the Baltimore Colts to stabilize the position. The Rams' defense, anchored by players like cornerback Nolan Cromwell, aimed to improve after allowing 332 points in 1981.

The Green Bay Packers, coached by Bart Starr in his eighth year, came off an 8–8 record in 1981, also missing the playoffs. The offense featured quarterback Lynn Dickey, wide receivers James Lofton and John Jefferson, and running back Eddie Lee Ivery. Lofton and Jefferson had combined for over 2,000 receiving yards in 1981, providing a potent passing attack. The Packers' defense sought to reduce the 361 points allowed the prior year.

The game was played at Milwaukee County Stadium, one of the Packers' home venues at the time, in front of 53,694 spectators. Green Bay held a slight edge in the recent series history, but Los Angeles led the all-time matchup 44–40 entering the game.

## Game summary

### First half

The Rams controlled the first half, scoring on their first five possessions while the Packers committed four turnovers. Los Angeles opened with a 4-yard rushing touchdown by Wendell Tyler, followed by a 32-yard field goal from Mike Lansford to lead 10–0 after the first quarter.

In the second quarter, Bert Jones connected with Mike Barber for an 8-yard touchdown pass, extending the lead to 17–0. Lansford added field goals of 29 and 28 yards, pushing the halftime score to 23–0. The Packers' offense struggled, with Lynn Dickey throwing two interceptions and fumbling twice. Green Bay managed only minimal yardage and no points in the half.

### Second half

The Packers mounted their comeback in the third quarter. Dickey led a drive culminating in a 4-yard touchdown pass to tight end Paul Coffman, making the score 23–7. After a Rams three-and-out, Green Bay scored again on a three-play drive: a 42-yard pass to Coffman set up a 3-yard rushing touchdown by Eddie Lee Ivery, narrowing the gap to 23–14.

In the fourth quarter, the Packers continued their surge. A 66-yard drive ended with a 15-yard touchdown pass from Dickey to James Lofton, giving Green Bay a 21–23 lead after the extra point from Jan Stenerud. On the ensuing kickoff, Packers linebacker Guy Prather forced a fumble from Rams returner Kermit Alexander, recovering the ball at the Los Angeles 10-yard line. Dickey then threw a 10-yard touchdown pass to Coffman, putting Green Bay ahead 28–23.

Late in the quarter, after a 19-yard run by fullback Mike Meade and a penalty, Ivery sealed the win with a 27-yard rushing touchdown, finalizing the score at 35–23. The Rams gained no first downs in the first 17 minutes of the second half and were held to four first downs overall after halftime. Green Bay's defense forced turnovers and limited Los Angeles to zero points in the final two quarters.

## Statistics

| Statistic | Los Angeles Rams | Green Bay Packers |
|------------|-------------------|---------------------|
| First downs | 12 | 22 |
| Total net yards | 271 | 377 |
| Rushing yards | 105 | 149 |
| Passing yards | 166 | 228 |
| Passing (Comp–Att–Int) | 17–31–2 | 17–27–3 |
| Time of possession | 29:40 | 30:20 |
| Turnovers | 3 | 6 |
| Penalties–yards | 11–88 | 2–15 |
| Sacks by–yards | 2–9 | 4–36 |
| Third-down efficiency | 4/16 | 4/8 |
| Field goals | 3/4 | 0/0 |

### Individual leaders

**Passing** 
* Rams: Bert Jones – 17/31, 202 yards, 1 TD, 2 INT 
* Packers: Lynn Dickey – 17/27, 237 yards, 3 TD, 3 INT 

**Rushing** 
* Rams: Wendell Tyler – 14 carries, 57 yards, 1 TD 
* Packers: Eddie Lee Ivery – 17 carries, 109 yards, 2 TD 

**Receiving** 
* Rams: Willie Miller – 3 receptions, 78 yards 
* Packers: John Jefferson – 6 receptions, 116 yards 

Source: 

## Aftermath and legacy

The Packers' victory propelled them to a 5–3–1 record in the strike-shortened season, securing a playoff spot as the third seed in the NFC. They advanced past the first round by defeating the St. Louis Cardinals but lost in the divisional round to the Dallas Cowboys. The Rams struggled post-strike, finishing 2–7 and missing the playoffs. Bert Jones retired after the season, and the team drafted Eric Dickerson in 1983 to bolster their running game.

The game remains significant in Packers history as their largest halftime comeback until 2013, when they overcame a 23-point deficit against the Dallas Cowboys. It exemplified the team's offensive potential under Dickey, who led the NFL in passing yards that season. The comeback also highlighted defensive improvements in the second half, a factor in Green Bay's playoff run.

The Packers' Texas-sized comeback on Sunday matched the biggest winning rally in franchise history. The previous victory came on Sept. 12, 1982, against the Los Angeles Rams.

Here are some highlights from that game played in front of 53,694 fans at County Stadium:

■The Packers scored 35 straight points after falling behing, 23-0, in the first half.

■Green Bay had five turnovers before halftime. Quarterback Lynn Dickey played a part in four of them, throwing two interceptions and losing two fumbles.

■Dickey bounced back by completing 8-of-12 passes for 157 yards and three touchdowns in the second half. Tight end Paul Coffman caught two of the scores and James Lofton the other.

■The Packers outgained the Rams in total yards, 377-271. Eddie Lee Ivery had 109 yards rushing for Green Bay.

■Green Bay had two touchdowns in the third quarter and three in the fourth.

■The Rams didn't have a first down for the first 17 minutes of the second half.

■On the kickoff following Dickey's TD pass to Lofton, Packers special teamer Guy Prather forced a fumble from Rams returner Robert Alexander. Prather recovered the ball, setting up a Dickey-to-Coffman score that gave the Packers the lead at 28-23.

![Image 3: 061003dickey_lynn215.jpg](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/private/t_editorial_landscape_mobile/f_auto/packers/fw5znhmgdaillhys8ltu.jpg)

As every card-carrying Packers aficionado well knows, Green Bay is the most titled team in the National Football League, with a dozen championships in hand.

In keeping with that imposing record, they also have a leg up on most of their rivals in their respective all-time series from the won-and-lost perspective...also known

as the bottom line.

The [St. Louis Rams](http://www.stlouisrams.com/), the opponents at hand, however, are a notable exception to the "rule."

The Rams, who will be displaying their current wares in Lambeau Field Sunday afternoon, lead the all-time rivalry, having won 44 games - four more than the Packers - in a series that dates back to 1937, when Sunday's invaders were in their original home and known as the Cleveland Rams.

To the Packers' understandable chagrin, the Rams also own the distinction of having dealt the Green and Gold the most decisive defeat in their postseason history - a 45-17 verdict forged in a dismal playoff at St. Louis on Jan. 20, 2002.

It was an indignity accentuated by the Missourians' larcenous defense, which intercepted six Brett Favre passes to accelerate the humbling process.

Fortunately, in turn, the Packers have had some singular moments against the Rams, chief among them their 28-7 Western Conference playoff victory at Milwaukee County Stadium in December of 1967 - eight days prior to what became the legendary "Ice Bowl" triumph over the [Dallas Cowboys](http://www.dallascowboys.com/).

And, beyond that memorable success, it was against the Rams that the Packers also enjoyed the greatest comeback in their long and distinguished annals.

Historically, it was to become a major highlight in the coaching career of Bart Starr, then in the eighth season of his nine-year tenure as head coach of the Packers.

The scene was Milwukee County Stadium and it was opening day of the 1982 NFL season (Sept. 12).

The Rams, with Bert Jones presiding at quarterback, moved out to a 23-0 halftime lead with the aid of three field goals by placekicker Mike Lansford as Los Angeles capitalized on a like number of Green Bay turnovers.

As the teams departed the field for their respective locker rooms at the intermission, the Packers were not aware that no Green Bay team trailing by as many as 23 points at halftime ever had come from behind to win a game.

Whatever the case, the substantial deficit had no apparent effect upon quarterback Lynn Dickey, who rebounded from an unsteady start to direct a remarkable second-half reversal - one punctuated by five touchdowns and 35 unanswered points en route to an astonishing 35-23 victory.

It was a tribute, in large part, to a suddenly tightfisted defense, which not only blanked the Rams over those last 30 minutes but held them to an exceedingly modest four first downs in the smothering process.

The second half renaissance began innocuously enough when, early in the third quarter, Dickey capped a 55-yard drive with a 4-yard scoring pass up the middle to tight end Paul Coffman. Following the first of Jan Stenerud's five conversions, the Packers still trailed the Rams, 23-7.

But not for long. Quickly forcing a punt after the subsequent kickoff, they were back in the end zone just three plays later.

Fullback Mike Meade launched the "drive" routinely with a 2-yard gain over right guard, after which Dickey promptly found Coffman with a 42-yard strike to the Rams' 3-yard line.

Running back Eddie Lee Ivery finished the project on the very next play, bolting off right tackle into the end zone.

The unfolding comeback was temporarily interrupted by Nolan Cromwell's interception of a Dickey pass near midfield, but the Rams shortly went empty-handed when a 51-yard Lansford field goal attempt veered wide left early in the fourth quarter.

The Packers continued their burgeoning resurgence, moving 66 yards in four plays to their third touchdown, 50 of them coming on a Dickey "bomb" to Coffman. Dickey then completed the process with a 15-yard strike to wideout James Lofton, then already well on his way to the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

The football fates then smiled warmly upon the Green and Gold.

Rams kickoff returner Kermit Alexander fumbled the succeeding kickoff, which was promptly recovered by Packers linebacker Guy Prather at the Los Angeles 10-yard line.

Whereupon Dickey took advantage with alacrity, firing a 10-yard bullseye to Coffman, who registered his second touchdown of the afternoon and propelled the Packers into their first lead of the day, 27-23.

A George Cumby interception at the Green Bay 30 then enabled the Packers to complete the comeback late in the fourth quarter. Meade's 19-yard burst up the middle, complemented by a 5-yard face mask penalty, was the key maneuver en route.

Two plays later, the artful Ivery slipped through the middle on a well-executed "draw" and cantered 27 yards to the game's final touchdown.

Stenerud added the 35th and final point of the record comeback with 3:06 remaining.

*Continuing an association with the team that is more than 55 years old, [Lee Remmel](https://www.packers.com/news/remmel-memorable-82-comeback-highlights-rams-series-2452938) was [named the first official Team Historian](https://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-1/packers-name-lee-remmel-team-historian/9eb331e1-5aa4-11df-a3b6-528cc843f916) of the Green Bay Packers in February 2004. The former Green Bay Press-Gazette reporter and Packers public relations director, Remmel will write regular columns for Packers.com as part of his new assignment.

In addition to those articles, Remmel will answer fan questions in a monthly Q&A column. To submit a question to Remmel, [click here.](https://www.packers.com/news/ask_lee_remmel/)*

9.content:
Published: Dec 18, 2013 at 04:20 AM

It was [a shocking setback](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299650/article/dallas-cowboys-continue-to-feature-a-flair-for-the-catastrophic) for America's so-called team, and [the ripple effect of this game](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299684/article/jason-garretts-job-at-risk-if-cowboys-miss-playoffs) might be felt for weeks to come. The [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) stormed out to a 26-3 halftime lead against what appeared for 30 minutes of play to be a totally overmatched [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) team that was without starting quarterback [Aaron Rodgers](https://www.nfl.com/player/aaronrodgers/2506363/profile) for the sixth consecutive game. Instead, Green Bay emerged from the locker room following halftime a rejuvenated bunch and rallied in the second half for the biggest comeback in franchise history in [a 37-36 win](http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013121512/2013/REG15/packers@cowboys#tab=recap&menu=highlights&recap=fullstory) in the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL)' own ballpark. It was one of the most exciting finishes of the season, and the events that led up to the victorious moment for Green Bay will be discussed and debated for a long time.

Here are the key moments before the moment:

### Cowboys build massive halftime lead

### Lacy sets tone for second half

**The play:**[Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) rookie running back [Eddie Lacy](https://www.nfl.com/player/eddielacy/2540168/profile) breaks free for a 60-yard gain on the first play from scrimmage in the second half.

**The aftermath:** A [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) team that was dormant in the first half suddenly sprang to life in an instant, with Lacy setting the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) up nicely for their first touchdown of the game. That score came three plays later, as quarterback [Matt Flynn](https://www.nfl.com/player/mattflynn/367/profile) hit receiver [Jordy Nelson](https://www.nfl.com/player/jordynelson/1032/profile) for [a 13-yard touchdown play](http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-cant-miss-plays/0ap2000000298577/WK-15-Can-t-Miss-Play-Nelson-snatches-it-from-Cowboy) that trimmed Dallas' lead to 26-10. It was an amazing play by Nelson, who snatched what could have been an interception away from [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) defensive back [Orlando Scandrick](https://www.nfl.com/player/orlandoscandrick/2307/profile) for the score.

### Packers' comeback is nearly complete

**The play:** Running back [James Starks](https://www.nfl.com/player/jamesstarks/497206/profile) catches a short pass from Flynn and goes 11 yards for a touchdown.

**The aftermath:** Starks' touchdown, coupled with tight end [Andrew Quarless' score](http://www.nfl.com/videos/green-bay-packers/0ap2000000298601/Quarless-3-yard-TD-reception) on the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB)' previous possession, cut the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL)' lead down to five at 29-24. With nearly 13 minutes still left to play, there was plenty of time for the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) to complete the improbable comeback.

### Cowboys strike back

**The play:** Quarterback [Tony Romo](https://www.nfl.com/player/tonyromo/2505354/profile) finds receiver [Dez Bryant](https://www.nfl.com/player/dezbryant/497278/profile) in the back of the end zone for a 5-yard touchdown play.

**The aftermath:** It was an amazing scoring snag by Bryant, who somehow managed to catch the ball among a host of [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) defenders and get two feet down before momentum carried him out of bounds. With less than eight minutes left, the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) were up 36-24 and perhaps had weathered the frantic second-half rally of the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB).

### Romo throws first of two costly interceptions

### Lacy puts the Pack on top

**The play:** With massive defensive linemen [Mike Daniels](https://www.nfl.com/player/mikedaniels/2532826/profile) and [B.J. Raji](https://www.nfl.com/player/b.j.raji/79631/profile) lined up at fullback, Lacy burst through for a 1-yard touchdown dive for the go-ahead score.

**The aftermath:** Lacy put an exclamation point on the score with an emphatic spike of the football. The comeback was complete and the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) led 37-36. A two-point conversion try failed, so all the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL) needed was a field goal to win. There was plenty of time for Romo and the Dallas offense to pull if off, too, as there was a minute and a half left on the game clock.

### The moment

**The play:**[Romo throws the second](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000298801/article/tony-romos-interceptions-cap-wild-packers-comeback) of two costly interceptions. This one to [Tramon Williams](https://www.nfl.com/player/tramonwilliams/2506789/profile) on a play that was initially ruled incomplete but then reversed following an instant-replay review.

**The aftermath:** A most implausible rally by the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB) in a frenzied second half was complete. As Green Bay maintained hope in its quest to reach the playoffs, Dallas missed out on a grand opportunity to take sole possession of first place in the NFC East. While the [Cowboys](https://www.nfl.com/teams/dallascowboys/profile?team=DAL)[were left with goats in the epic collapse](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299442/article/tony-romo-gets-heat-what-about-monte-kiffin-jason-garrett), the [Packers](https://www.nfl.com/teams/greenbaypackers/profile?team=GB)' Flynn [achieved hero status](http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap2000000299492/article/green-bay-packers-quarterback-matt-flynn-hero) in what has been a roller-coaster 2013 for the quarterback.
